title: Corpus-Context Transfer — Capability Evidence Porting Across Serum States
goal: Prove the producer can safely transfer verified capabilities from native Serum context to corpus-derived Serum context without silent assumptions
critical_principle: Parameter name/index matching ≠ safe transfer. Evidence context must also match.

transfer_framework.rule_1_name_index_not_sufficient: Same parameter name and index across contexts does not guarantee the control is safe to transfer. The parameter may have different ranges, different behavior, or different semantic meaning in different Serum preset states.
transfer_framework.rule_2_evidence_context_matters: Each capability's evidence comes from a specific context (native/clean Serum state discovered in 16.5.61-64). Transfer requires independent verification that the context still applies in the target state.
rule_3_three_transfer_outcomes: TRANSFERRED: Evidence context fully applies; control works identically in corpus context
CONTEXT_LIMITED: Evidence applies but with caveats (e.g., some parameters constrained differently)
REFUSED: Evidence context does not apply; transfer unsafe

example_row.evidence_context: Native Serum (fresh state, idx 1 = A Level)
example_row.transfer_status: TRANSFERRED (if ranges match and behavior is identical)
example_row.reason: Parameter exists at same index with same name and range in both contexts. Evidence of OSC1.Volume control from 16.5.61-64 applies here.

capabilities_to_transfer.evidence_behavior: ABSOLUTE: write value 0-1 → direct output level
ABSOLUTE: write value 0.1 → 86 Hz, write value 0.5 (est.) → ~4000 Hz

phase_1_load_corpus_context.action: Load a different Serum preset (corpus-derived, not native/clean state)
phase_1_load_corpus_context.goal: Establish a sufficiently different starting state from 16.5.64
phase_1_load_corpus_context.example: A preset with different oscillator volumes, filter settings, envelope times

phase_2_build_transfer_matrix.action: For each of the 5 capabilities, verify it exists in corpus context with matching properties

phase_3_apply_bass_patch_in_corpus_conte.action: Compile the same bass intents in corpus context
phase_3_apply_bass_patch_in_corpus_conte.admission_gate: Only admitted capabilities from transfer matrix

phase_4_execute_and_verify.action: Execute MCP batch, readback, compare to native context result
verification: Readback matches written values (same tolerance as 16.5.64)
Sonic character comparable to native bass patch

phase_5_report_transfer_outcome.outcome_matrix: Which capabilities TRANSFERRED, which CONTEXT_LIMITED, which REFUSED
phase_5_report_transfer_outcome.sonic_comparison: Does corpus-derived bass sound similar to native bass?

prerequisite: Load corpus-derived Serum state (not the native clean state from 16.5.64). This should be a different preset or starting configuration.
next_steps_after_16_5_65: 16.5.66 — Arrangement Brief: Define bass/pad/lead roles, timing, transitions
16.5.67 — MIDI Source Compiler: Multi-instrument patch construction from semantic goals
16.5.68+ — Full arrangement production: Use typed-intent layer across all three instrument roles

theoretical_outcome.best_case_all_transferred: All 5 bass capabilities transfer cleanly. Producer can apply 16.5.62-64 bass patch to any Serum state with identical character.
theoretical_outcome.partial_transfer_context_limited: Some capabilities transfer, others require constraint warnings (e.g., 'Volume maxed in this context, cannot go louder'). Producer uses only the safe subset.
theoretical_outcome.some_refused: A capability that works in native context does not apply in corpus context (e.g., Filter1.On already off and cannot be toggled). Producer refuses to apply it and documents why.
theoretical_outcome.interpretation: In all cases, the test proves the producer makes evidence-based transfer decisions, not guesses.

summary: 16.5.65 bridges from 'we proved it works on Serum state A' (16.5.61-64) to 'we can reliably apply it to Serum state B' (any corpus context). The transfer framework ensures each capability is re-validated before reuse, preventing silent misapplications across different Serum starting states.
